descriptions.shortDescription: Construction project management and built environment administration for Nextcloud.
descriptions.longDescription: Buildiq is a project management and administration application for the built environment, built on Nextcloud and Open Register. It supports construction project management, permit tracking, and built-environment administration for municipalities and construction organisations. Buildiq integrates with Dutch government standards and open data sources for the built environment.
features: Integration with Dutch government open data

descriptions.longDescription: Buildiq is een projectbeheers- en administratietoepassing voor de gebouwde omgeving, gebouwd op Nextcloud en Open Register. Het ondersteunt bouwprojectbeheer, vergunningenbewaking en omgevingsadministratie voor gemeenten en bouworganisaties. Buildiq integreert met Nederlandse overheidsstandaarden en open databronnen voor de gebouwde omgeving.
features: Integratie met open data van de Nederlandse overheid

results.title: Project health (CHAOSS)

metrics.name: Contributor Absence Factor
metrics.explanation: The fewest people who together made half of the commits on the default branch in the last 12 months, of the 100 contributors GitHub reports, among 6 human contributors. At 1 the project depends on a single person. Bots are left out; one person with several accounts or addresses counts more than once.

metrics.name: Organizational Diversity
metrics.explanation: Organisations are told apart by the email domain of the latest 300 commits of the last 12 months (246 commits by people, after the .mailmap) and, for a personal or hidden address, by the company on the author's public profile. The largest is conduction.nl (4 authors), with 100% of the 246 commits whose organisation is known; 0% of the commits come from 0 of 4 authors whose organisation stays unknown. Only these counts are kept, no names, addresses or companies; an organisation is named only when several authors share it.

metrics.name: Change Request Closure Ratio
metrics.explanation: 1,154 change requests were closed (merged or not) and 1,223 opened in the last 90 days, bots included. Below 1 the open backlog grows; above 1 it shrinks.

metrics.name: Time to First Response
metrics.explanation: None of the 15 latest change requests opened by people between 2026-08-22 and 2026-11-13 got a comment or review from anyone but its author.

metrics.name: Issue Response Time
metrics.explanation: None of the 8 latest issues opened by people between 2026-08-22 and 2026-11-13 got a comment from anyone but its author.

metrics.name: Release Frequency
metrics.explanation: 3 final releases were published in the last 12 months, about one every 122 days, counted from the GitHub releases. The latest final release is from 2026-09-06. Besides these, 267 pre-releases were published; they are not counted. Drafts and pre-releases are left out.

Burn down phpmd.baseline.xml (174 entries, 48 files) now that composer phpmd is a real gate

ExportService::buildScaffoldMap() has no production caller — its call site was never rescued from Codeberg
Suppression & baseline audit: what the green PHPMD number hides
SetupController's six @spec anchors point at headings that don't exist — and the correct fix drags 7 uncovered e2e scenarios with it
Issue Triage has NEVER succeeded — 34 runs, 0 passes, since 2026-07-23 (PROJECT_TOKEN is empty)
gate-58: 14 networkidle waits are real, but the suggested swap is a no-op — needs per-site element waits and a live instance
gate-61: two listeners run an unbounded findAll() on the object write path (ADR-078) — the fix needs an architecture decision
newman-seed-command is an && chain and the Newman leg is disabled, so the seed has never been exercised
diff endpoint implements a ref grammar the spec does not define (REQ-OBV-005: slug / current: / history:, controller: draft | UUID)
Two save-as-template scenarios were counted as e2e-covered by a test whose own comment says it proves neither
Spec drift: scenarios describing surfaces the product does not have — and stale skip reasons that are now writable
page-designer-ui: 7 tests CI never runs, 14 dangling anchors, and 10 scenarios excluded because 'another spec's Playwright tests cover it'
Two openbuild-runtime scenarios skip for fixture users that globalSetup already provisions

notes: Measured over the open issues and the issues closed in the last 90 days, in working days (Monday to Friday, Europe/Amsterdam, without Dutch public holidays).

Vulnerabilities are read from the published GitHub security advisories, from draft to publication. Their response time, unpublished advisories and Dependabot alerts need admin rights and are not measured.
No issue carries a blocking label (such as blocker or critical), so every bug counts as an other bug.
